title: Eosinophil-to-neutrophil balance did not improve cross-cycle FEV1/FVC prediction beyond nonlinear separate counts
abstract: A prespecified representation test fitted models in 3,560 NHANES 2007–2008 adults and transferred them without refitting to 3,996 NHANES 2009–2010 adults. Adding a spline of the log eosinophil-to-neutrophil ratio to demographics, smoking, anthropometry and separate count splines changed FEV1/FVC RMSE from 0.067206 to 0.067269. Delta MSE was 0.00000837 (target-participant bootstrap 95% interval 0.00000086 to 0.00001810). Source-refit plus target bootstrap uncertainty spanned zero. Weighted, quality and representation challenges did not support incremental benefit. These separately sampled survey releases share a protocol and are not independent clinical programmes. This negative result tests a deterministic feature representation, not the presence or absence of eosinophilic airway biology.
